entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Drest VII was the king of the Picts from 724 until 726, succeeding Nechtan mac Der-Ilei who abdicated and entered a monastery.

    Drest VII played a pivotal role in the governance of the Pictish Kingdom, a pre-Celtic, Iron Age culture in Scotland.

    His reign was marked by significant events, including the Battle of Dumbarton Rock in 726, where the Picts were defeated by the Kingdom of Dalriada.

    The legacy of Drest VII can be seen in the continued influence of the Pictish culture on Scottish identity and the ongoing debate about the origins of the Kingdom of Scotland.

    As he died in 729 CE, Drest VII left behind a complex and multifaceted historical record, with his successors struggling to maintain the unity and power of the Pictish Kingdom.
